title: Move Regex::new out of the loop with LazyLock
summary: Stop recompiling a regex for every line by putting it in a std::sync::LazyLock static, and trip the unwrap in a test first.

turns.user: log parsing batch is slow. profiler says Regex::new is near the top

assistant.body: Here's what is going on: Regex::new compiles the pattern into an automaton, which is expensive, and the loop does it again for every line. Put the Regex in a std::sync::LazyLock static instead. It is compiled once, on first use, and then shared by every thread. Since Rust 1.80 this is in the standard library, so neither once_cell nor lazy_static is needed.

turns.user: theres an unwrap inside the static. dont want that panicking in prod

assistant.body: Great question! The pattern is a fixed literal, so if it is broken it panics the same way every time. Call LazyLock::force from a test and that compile runs in CI before it can ever run in production.
